subsystems.name: Quantum sensor payload
subsystems.role: measures tiny spacetime curvature or quantum decoherence effects.

subsystems.name: Drag-free reference system
subsystems.role: keeps test masses in free fall, isolated from solar radiation pressure and other non-gravitational forces.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic and vacuum enclosure
subsystems.role: reduces thermal noise and gas collisions that would swamp quantum signals.

subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus and orbit
subsystems.role: provides power, pointing, and communications in a quiet environment.

subsystems.name: Quantum link and clock
subsystems.role: distributes entangled photons or compares optical clocks to test quantum gravity predictions.

subsystems.name: Data and modelling pipeline
subsystems.role: extracts a faint signal from noise and compares it to theoretical predictions.

buildSteps.title: Choose a measurable observable
buildSteps.detail: Quantum gravity has no agreed experimental signature, so a mission must target something testable — such as decoherence of entangled particles, a violation of the equivalence principle, or spacetime fluctuations.

buildSteps.title: Develop and qualify quantum sensors
buildSteps.detail: Atom interferometers or optomechanical devices are built and tested in drop towers and on parabolic flights to prove they survive launch and work in free fall.

buildSteps.title: Build the drag-free spacecraft
buildSteps.detail: Test masses are suspended electrostatically and micro-thrusters cancel all non-gravitational forces, as first demonstrated by LISA Pathfinder.

buildSteps.title: Integrate cryogenics and vacuum
buildSteps.detail: Sensors are cooled to cryogenic temperatures and sealed in a high vacuum to suppress thermal and gas noise.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and test the satellite
buildSteps.detail: Payload and bus are integrated, then shaken and baked in thermal-vacuum chambers to space-qualify the whole system.

buildSteps.title: Launch and commission
buildSteps.detail: The satellite is placed in a high Earth orbit or a heliocentric orbit far from Earth's vibrations and gravity gradients, then its instruments are calibrated.

buildSteps.title: Operate and analyse
buildSteps.detail: Long-duration runs collect data, which is compared with predictions from candidate quantum gravity theories to see if any signal stands out.

prerequisites.why: atom interferometers have flown on sounding rockets, but not yet on long-duration satellites.
LISA Pathfinder proved test masses can be kept in near-perfect free fall.
satellites have distributed entangled photons over thousands of kilometres, but not with the stability needed for gravity tests.
space clocks exist, but quantum gravity tests need stability and accuracy still under development.
without a clear, testable number from quantum gravity theory, a mission cannot know what signal to look for.

pathway.milestone: laboratory and drop-tower tests of quantum sensors, plus LISA Pathfinder's drag-free demonstration
pathway.unlocks: confidence that precision quantum experiments can work in free fall.

pathway.milestone: a small satellite testing one quantum gravity effect, such as equivalence-principle violation or entanglement decoherence
pathway.unlocks: the first space-based constraints on quantum gravity models.

pathway.milestone: a larger mission combining quantum sensors, optical clocks and long-distance entanglement
pathway.unlocks: overlapping tests that can rule out whole classes of theories.
direct experimental guidance for unifying general relativity and quantum mechanics.
